To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have identified a novel epithelial-expressing ETS gene, named ELF3, which may have a role in epithelial tumorigenesis.

we have identified a novel member of the ETS family of transcription factors and characterized its expression in tissues and tumors, and have localized it to a region of the human genome that is amplified in several epithelial tumors, suggesting its involvement in tumor development.

1) we identify a novel Ets family member, Elf3, and present its cDNA sequence, 2) Elf3 has an alternatively spiced transcript in the mouse, 3) Elf3 is expressed in epithelial cells and tissues, 4) the human ELF3 gene maps to 1q31-32, 5) the ELF3 gene is amplified in epithelially derived cancers, 6) ELF3 is overexpressed in epithelial cancers
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification, characterization and mapping of the human and murine ELF3 genes and their tissue-specific expression.
the identification and characterization of a novel ETS member, ELF3.
identification of novel ETS family genes and characterization of their structure, organization and expression.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
ELF3 is a novel ETS gene that is specifically expressed in epithelial organs and cell lines.
ELF3 is a novel member of the ETS family of transcription factors that has an interesting tissue distribution, and is expressed in epithelial cell types.
ELF3 is a novel epithelial-exposed ETS gene with potential implications in cancer.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have identified a novel ETS gene, Elf3, which is expressed in epithelial organs and is over-expressed in lung tumors.
we have identified a novel ETS gene, Elf3, that has a unique pattern of expression, and may be involved in epithelial tumors.
ELF3 is a new member of the ETS family of transcription factors.
The main takeaway from our work is that
ELF3 is expressed in epithelial organs and epithelial cell lines, but not in hematopoietically derived organs or hematopoietic cell lines.
